Nice work. The tickets will soon sell for well over a thousand dollars each on StubHub. Ticket prices have gone much higher because dynamic pricing puts money in concert performer or team/athlete’s hands instead of scalpers.


Polymarket (@Polymarket)

JUST IN: New York City mayor, Zohran Mamdani, secures 1,000 $50 tickets to World Cup games at MetLife Stadium for NYC residents.



— https://nitter.net/Polymarket/status/2057438983924170830#m

This trend will likely accelerate as the wealthiest tax payers continue to flee NY, CA, and IL, often relocating to TN, FL and Texas. This will increase the taxing doom spiral in blue states and lessen the costs in red states, which will continue to accelerate moves.

The coaches vs (some) fans split on an expanded college football playoff is interesting. Coaches know they will be judged on making the playoff or not. Meanwhile the same fans who don’t want an expanded playoff will demand their coaches be fired if they don’t make the playoff.

Tennessee, Florida and Texas are replacing California, New York and Illinois as the cultural and economic hubs of America. No state income tax vs highest state income taxes in the country. Pay attention to this over next generation, it’s a monster story. (2030 census per @axios).

Encourage everyone to watch the full @JeffBezos interview on @cnbc. He was fantastic. Here he is discussing NYC spending $44k per student and still getting awful results and comparing it to Amazon.

Video

Coach O has never been a college coach when you could legally pay players. Buckle up!


LSU Football (@LSUfootball)

Ed Orgeron is returning to LSU and will serve as the special assistant to recruiting and defense for the Tigers





— https://nitter.net/LSUfootball/status/2057283568821211603#m

Three things to make college football bigger & better: 1. No conference title games. 2. Expanded playoff so all title contenders qualify. (Notre Dame could have won title last year.) 3. Multiple networks — ESPN, Fox, NBC & CBS all with playoff games.

Jeff Bezos says we don’t have a revenue problem with taxes. We have a spending problem. He’s 100% right. Listen to his math.

This is a perfect distillation of sports media cowardice and failure. A judgement call on track celebrations is covered ad infinitum, but a boy winning multiple girl’s track titles is mostly ignored by sports media. Which is more indefensible? The boy winning!

There’s more sports media outrage — and coverage — over a high school track celebration costing a boy’s team a track state title in North Carolina than there is a boy winning multiple state titles in girl’s track in California.
